reason: Final dependency and axiom-contract audit: Because C_H(Z)=H, the Brauer homomorphism Br_Z on (kH)^Z=kH is the identity coefficient projection, hence Br_Z(c)=c is nonzero. Maximal Brauer support puts Z inside a conjugate of any defect group D of c. Since Z is central, conjugating that containment back leaves Z fixed, so Z<=D. This also proves that for a p-element u, block induction from C_G(u) is defined for every local block: its defect groups contain <u>, hence their G-centralizers lie in C_G(u). AC is inherited exactly from the published maximal-Brauer-support contract through its finite-dimensional Krull-Schmidt supplier; the displayed finite subgroup argument adds no choice. Evidence inspected: Craven, The Brauer Correspondence, Lemma 1.2 and §1.3, pp. 2 and 7–9; Meierfrankenfeld, MTH 912 Class Notes, §§6.6–6.7, pp. 156–165.
